sections.overview: The Red Crossbill is a finch of conifer forests across the Northern Hemisphere, where it tracks changing cone crops.
sections.identification: Its mandible tips cross, helping it pry open cone scales; adult males are usually red, while females are greenish or yellowish.
sections.habitat: It uses natural and planted conifer woods, especially where mature cones are available.
sections.diet: Conifer seeds are its main food, extracted from cones with the crossed bill; adults also feed seeds to their chicks.
sections.behavior: Its movements are nomadic and can carry it far from its usual range when local cone crops fail.
sections.reproduction: Breeding is flexible and may occur in any season when cone seeds are sufficiently abundant to support a brood.
sections.ecology: Cornell notes that Red Crossbill populations form distinct ecological or vocal “types”, but whether some merit species status remains unsettled; this caution also matters when comparing it with other crossbills.
sections.conservation: The consulted species account describes it as widespread and not globally threatened; local populations may still differ.
